sofia: Nightly harness finished — found a kernel-pick flip affecting ampere_midseq (seq ~512). p95 reg ~8% on candidate-k1. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/nightly/4309876543/index.html :thinking_face:
perf-bot: nightly-run 4309876543 completed — 1 regression flagged, 3 flaky tests. See summary & raw logs above.
andre: Can you paste the microbench numbers from the run?
sofia: Sure — microbench delta for candidate-k1 vs baseline-k0:
```
median: 4.2ms -> 4.5ms (+7.1%)
p95:   12.1ms -> 13.1ms (+8.3%)
cache_miss_rate: 2% -> 18% (per-sample KV probe)
commit: ab12f3c -> bc34d5e
configuration: batch-path-elasticity=on, kv-cache-policy=adaptive
```
matt: Hmm. That cache_miss_rate jump smells like a batching fallback into the long-tail path. Did the autotuner change picks?
julian: We did tweak architecture-weighting last week to bias against heavy-gpu memory kernels (elasticity score). Might be related.
sofia: Autotune log excerpt shows score_shift:+0.12 for ampere which bumped kv-opt-v2 above kv-opt-v1 at seq=512. Exact log: `autopick: ampere seq512 candidate=kv-opt-v2 score=0.87 (+0.12)`
andre: Repro steps?
sofia: Repro command I used locally:
```
./tools/prober --model gargantua-8b --seq 512 --arch ampere --kitchen candidate-k1.json --runs 2000 --profile micro
```
sofia: Local prober confirms miss spike; microprobe log included in artifact.
matt: Quick triage proposal:
1) temporarily disable elasticity weighting for ampere midseq picks
2) run focused microbench (seq 256/512/1024) with fixed batch-path to isolate fallback
3) run a canary nightly with revert and monitor p95 and KV miss
julian: I'll author config change to gate elasticity per-arch. Pushing draft now, cc @ci-bot.
ci-bot: pipeline redwood/autotune-configs #7842 started; jobs: lint -> unit -> integration -> deploy-canary.
sofia: Also attaching flamegraph for a representative request: s3://redwood-perf/nightly/4309876543/flame-k1.svg — main hotspots in kv_cache::refill and batch_scheduler::fallback.
sofia: TL;DR: autotuner weighting change caused selection of a kernel that degrades p95 at midseq on ampere by increasing KV cache refill frequency because of altered batching behavior. Plan: revert weighting for ampere midseq, run microbench + canary, then re-evaluate elasticity heuristic with additional penalty for cache-miss amplification.
andre: Acknowledge. I'll prepare the cherry-pick and run the focused microbench after the config rollback lands.
matt: If the rollback reduces p95, we should add a regression test to CI that monitors cache_miss_rate for canonical midseq samples.
sofia: Agreed — filing a perf ticket and adding to nightly smoke list. :thumbsup:
